questions.stem: The table shows some properties of four substances, P, Q, R and S. Use the information in the table to answer the following questions. You may use each letter once, more than once or not at all. Choose a substance that:

parts.label: a
parts.text: is a solid at $ 3 0 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ A substance P B substance Q C substance R D substance S

parts.label: b
parts.text: is a liquid at $ 2 5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}. $ A substance P B substance Q C substance R D substance S

parts.label: c
parts.text: is an ionic compound. A substance P B substance Q C substance R A substance P D substance S B substance Q

parts.label: d
parts.text: is a metal. C substance R D substance S

questions.stem: This is a method used to measure the solubility of a solid in water: add an excess of solid to some water in a boiling tube and stir measure the temperature of the saturated solution formed weigh an empty evaporating basin pour some of the saturated solution into the evaporating basin weigh the basin and contents heat the evaporating basin to remove all of the water weigh the evaporating basin and remaining solid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The table shows the results of an experiment using this method. Calculate the mass of solid obtained and the mass of water removed. mass of water = ... g

parts.label: b
parts.text: In another experiment, at a different temperature, the mass of solid obtained is 10.5 g and the mass of water removed is 16.8 g. Calculate the solubility of the solid, in g per 100 g of water, at this temperature. solubility = g per 100 g of water

parts.label: c
parts.text: If the evaporating basin is heated too strongly some of the solid decomposes to form a gas. Explain how this strong heating would affect the value of the calculated solubility of the solid.

questions.stem: Astatine, bromine, chlorine, fluorine and iodine are all halogens. They are found in Group 7 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Predict which halogen has the lightest colour.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name a halogen that is a solid at room temperature.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Bromine can be obtained from the bromide ions in sea water. Chlorine is bubbled into sea water. The chlorine oxidises the bromide ions to bromine atoms. The bromine atoms then form bromine molecules.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Complete the equation to show how bromine atoms are formed from bromide ions. $\mathrm {C l} _ {2} + \dots \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {B r} ^ {-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {C l} ^ {-} + \dots \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {B r}$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State why this reaction is described as the oxidation of bromide ions.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Write an equation to show how bromine atoms form bromine molecules.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Boron and fluorine form a covalent compound that has the molecular formula $ \mathrm{B F}_{3} $ Draw a dot-and-cross diagram to show the arrangement of the outer electrons in a molecule of $ \mathrm{B F}_{3} $ Use crosses (X) to represent the outer electrons of boron. Use dots (•) to represent the outer electrons of fluorine.

questions.stem: A technician finds a white solid in an unlabelled beaker. She knows that the solid is one of the following substances: potassium chloride potassium sulfate sodium chloride sodium sulfate. Describe how the technician can use chemical tests to identify the solid in the beaker.

Zinc metal is obtained from sulfide ores. The most common ore of zinc is sphalerite, which contains zinc sulfide (ZnS) and a small amount of cadmium sulfide (CdS). The stages involved in the extraction of zinc from sphalerite are: Stage1 Sphalerite is strongly heated in air. $2 \mathrm {Z n S} (\mathrm {s}) + 3 \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {Z n O} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {S O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ $2 \mathrm {C d S} (\mathrm {s}) + 3 \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {C d O} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {S O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ Stage 2 The mixture of oxides is reacted with sulfuric acid. $\mathrm {Z n O (s)} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {Z n S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I})$ $\mathrm {C d O (s)} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {C d S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O (l)}$ Stage 3 Zinc dust is added to the solution containing zinc sulfate and cadmium sulfate to remove the cadmium ions. $\mathrm {C d} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {Z n} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow \mathrm {C d} (\mathrm {s}) + \mathrm {Z n} ^ {2 +} (\mathrm {a q})$ Stage 4 The solid cadmium is filtered off and the pure zinc sulfate solution is electrolysed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State how the reaction in stage 3 shows that zinc is more reactive than cadmium.

parts.label: b
parts.text: During the electrolysis in stage 4, zinc is deposited on the cathode. Write an ionic half-equation for the reaction that occurs.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Complete the ionic half-equation for the reaction occurring at the anode. $\dots \dots H _ {2} O \rightarrow \dots \dots H ^ {+} + O _ {2} + \dots \dots e ^ {-}$

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Explain how the pH of the solution surrounding the anode changes during the electrolysis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Zinc is mixed with copper to make the alloy brass. Explain why brass is harder than pure copper.

questions.stem: The mineral nesquehonite is a form of hydrated magnesium carbonate. The formula, $ \mathrm{M g C O_{3}. x H_{2} O} $ , shows that nesquehonite contains water of crystallisation. When a sample of nesquohonite is heated gently, the water of crystallisation is given off and anhydrous magnesium carbonate is left. Six students are each given a sample of nesquehonite of mass 6.1 g. The students heat their samples for different times. The samples are then allowed to cool before being reweighed. The table shows their results.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Plot these results on the grid provided. The last two points have been plotted for you. Draw a straight line of best fit for the points you have plotted. mass of sample after heating / g

parts.label: b
parts.text: Predict the mass of sample remaining after heating for 2.5 minutes. Show on the graph how you obtain your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State why the last two masses in the table are exactly the same.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A sample of nesquehonite contains 1.68 g of $ \mathrm{M g C O_{3}} $ and 1.08 g of $ \mathrm{H_{2}O}. $ Calculate the value of x in the formula $ \mathrm{M g C O_{3}. x H_{2}O} $ $ [ M_{r} $ of $ \mathrm{M g C O_{3}} $ = 84; $ M_{r} $ of $ \mathrm{H_{2}O}=18] $

parts.label: e
parts.text: When anhydrous magnesium carbonate is heated strongly, it decomposes. The equation for the reaction is: $\mathrm {M g C O} _ {3} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g O} (\mathrm {s}) + \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide formed in $ cm^{3} $ , at rtp, when 4.2 g of anhydrous magnesium carbonate are completely decomposed. $ [ M_{r} $ of $ MgCO_{3}=84] $ [Assume that the molar volume at rtp of carbon dioxide is $ 24\mathrm{d m}^{3} $ ]

questions.stem: Ammonia is manufactured on a large scale and is used to make fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate $ \mathrm{(N H_{4} N O_{3})}. $

parts.label: a
parts.text: The first stage in the manufacture of ammonium nitrate is to react ammonia gas with oxygen gas. $4 \mathrm {N H} _ {3} (\mathrm {g}) + 5 \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons 4 \mathrm {N O} (\mathrm {g}) + 6 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {g}) \quad \Delta H = - 9 0 7 \mathrm {k J / m o l}$ The reaction is carried out at a pressure of about 10 atm and at a temperature of $ 8 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ , in the presence of a catalyst. If the mixture is left for long enough in a sealed container, the reaction reaches a position of dynamic equilibrium. Graph A shows how the percentage of nitrogen monoxide (NO) in the equilibrium mixture varies with temperature at constant pressure. Graph B shows how the percentage of nitrogen monoxide (NO) in the equilibrium mixture varies with pressure at constant temperature.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Explain why the percentage of NO at equilibrium decreases in each case.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain why the use of a catalyst has no effect on the position of equilibrium in a reversible reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The second stage in the manufacture of ammonium nitrate is to convert the nitrogen monoxide into nitric acid. The nitric acid is then reacted with concentrated aqueous ammonia as shown in this equation. $\mathrm {H N O} _ {3} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {N H} _ {3} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {N H} _ {4} \mathrm {N O} _ {3} (\mathrm {a q})$

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State, in terms of proton transfer, why this reaction is classified as an acid-base reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Calculate the volume of $ 1 4. 8 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ aqueous ammonia that is required to exactly neutralise $ 1 5 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of a solution of nitric acid of concentration $ 1 5. 8 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $

questions.stem: Polymers can be classified as addition polymers or condensation polymers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An addition polymer can be formed from the monomer $ \mathrm{C H_{2}=C H C l} $

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Name this monomer.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Name the addition polymer formed from this monomer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The diagram shows the repeat unit of a different addition polymer. Draw the displayed formula of the monomer used to make this polymer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Polyesters are condensation polymers. The structures of two monomers that are used to make a polyester are: HO—CH $ _{2} $ CH $ _{2} $ —OH

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Draw the structure of the repeat unit of the polyester formed from these two monomers.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Identify the small molecule formed when these two monomers form the polyester.

questions.stem: Grapes contain glucose that can be fermented to make ethanol.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The grapes are collected and crushed to produce an aqueous solution containing glucose. Yeast is added to the solution and the mixture is left to ferment at a temperature of about $ 3 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ in the absence of air.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: State why yeast is added.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain why another organic compound may also be formed if fermentation is carried out in the presence of air.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Explain why $ 3 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ is considered to be an optimum temperature for this reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethanol can also be manufactured by reacting ethene with steam.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Write the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: State two conditions used for this reaction in industry.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Grapes also contain esters. The formula of an ester is shown. Deduce the name of the carboxylic acid and the alcohol that can react together to make this ester. carboxylic acid alcohol..
